record.original_question: Establish the relationship between continuum elasticity theory and atomistic models, including whether elasticity can be derived from quantum, density-functional, Thomas-Fermi, or interatomic-potential models; what limiting energy and function space arise from atomistic minimizers; and how atomistic-continuum matching methods such as quasicontinuum schemes can be rigorously understood.

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Establish the status of elasticity theory with respect to atomistic models.
The second approach is to consider the true minimizers of the discrete problems, and to try to understand what functional their limit minimizes.
A rigorous understanding of such methods is lacking.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a crystalline solid modeled as a discrete configuration of atoms occupying, in a reference state, the lattice $\varepsilon \mathbb{Z}^d \cap \Omega$ (or a more general Bravais/multilattice) inside a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, where $\varepsilon>0$ is the interatomic spacing. To each deformation $y:\varepsilon\mathbb{Z}^d\cap\Omega \to \mathbb{R}^d$ associate a discrete energy $E_\varepsilon(y)$ derived from one of the following atomistic descriptions:
(i) a quantum many-body Schrödinger Hamiltonian for nuclei and electrons;
(ii) a Kohn–Sham or Hartree–Fock density-functional energy;
(iii) a Thomas–Fermi (or Thomas–Fermi–von Weizsäcker) functional;
(iv) a classical interatomic potential energy $E_\varepsilon(y)=\sum_{i} V_i\bigl(\{y(x_j)-y(x_i)\}_{j}\bigr)$ involving pair, three-body, or many-body interactions (e.g. Lennard–Jones, embedded-atom, Stillinger–Weber).

Address rigorously the following three coupled questions.

1. (Derivation of continuum elasticity.) For each class of atomistic model above, identify a continuum elastic energy functional
$$E(u)=\int_\Omega W(\nabla u(x))\,dx$$
(or its appropriate non-simple/higher-gradient generalization) and a function space $X$ of admissible deformations $u:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $E_\varepsilon \xrightarrow{\Gamma} E$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ in a suitable topology, and characterize the stored-energy density $W$ (e.g. via the Cauchy–Born rule $W(F)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{N^d}\min E_{\rm cell}(F\cdot\,\cdot\,)$) together with its domain of validity (small strains, frame indifference, material symmetry, possible loss of validity under large or non-rank-one strains).

2. (Limits of true minimizers.) Let $y_\varepsilon$ be a sequence of (almost) minimizers of $E_\varepsilon$ subject to prescribed boundary or loading data. Determine the limiting functional $\mathcal{F}$ and function space $X^*$ (which may differ from $X$ above and may incorporate defects: dislocations, cracks, grain boundaries, or plastic slip) such that, up to subsequence, $y_\varepsilon \to u$ in $X^*$ and $u$ minimizes $\mathcal{F}$, and identify the mechanism by which microstructure, defects, or singular measures arise in $\mathcal{F}$.

3. (Quasicontinuum coupling.) Formulate quasicontinuum-type atomistic-to-continuum coupling schemes (energy-based, force-based, blended, or ghost-force-free variants) in which the atomistic energy is retained in a small subdomain while a Cauchy–Born continuum approximation is used elsewhere, and establish: (a) consistency (truncation/coupling error), (b) stability of the linearized coupled operator uniformly in $\varepsilon$ and in the size of the atomistic region, and (c) optimal a priori and a posteriori error estimates between the coupled solution and the fully atomistic minimizer in the presence of typical defects (point defects, dislocations, cracks).

Provide a unified rigorous theory, valid for at least one of the model classes (i)–(iv), that simultaneously answers (1), (2), and (3).
artifact.status_search_result: Significant partial results exist: Γ-convergence derivations of nonlinear elasticity from pair interactions (Alicandro–Cicalese, Friesecke–Theil), rigorous plate theory (Friesecke–James–Müller), Cauchy–Born validity in small-strain regimes (E–Ming, Conti–Dolzmann–Kirchheim–Müller), and convergence/error analyses of quasicontinuum methods (Ortner, Luskin, Süli, and collaborators), including blended force-based schemes for multilattices with defects. However, a unified rigorous derivation starting from quantum, DFT, or Thomas–Fermi models, a complete characterization of limits of true atomistic minimizers in the presence of generic defects, and a fully general convergence theory for atomistic/continuum coupling remain open active research areas.

status_evidence.title: Atomistic-to-continuum coupling
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of rigorous results and remaining open issues in atomistic-to-continuum coupling methods.
status_evidence.claim: Atomistic/continuum coupling is a subject of ongoing rigorous analysis with both progress and open questions.

status_evidence.title: Atomistic to Continuum limits for computational materials science
status_evidence.snippet: Mathematical results providing elements of a rigorous basis for multiscale computations in materials science.
status_evidence.claim: Partial rigorous derivations of continuum models from atomistic ones exist.

status_evidence.title: Force-based atomistic/continuum blending for multilattices
status_evidence.snippet: Blended force-based quasicontinuum method with rigorous error estimates for multilattices with point defects.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress provides rigorous error estimates for QC-type coupling in defect settings.

status_evidence.title: Analysis of a quasicontinuum method in one dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Rigorous one-dimensional analysis of the quasicontinuum method.
status_evidence.claim: Rigorous analysis is available in 1D; higher-dimensional generality is incomplete.
